meanings.note: Used with لـ for the addressee: قلت للسائق ('I told the driver').

examples.trans: I told you from the beginning.
What did the principal say?

meanings.note: With لـ + الـ, becomes للسائق ('to the bus driver').

examples.trans: I told the driver to wait for me.
The bus driver arrived on time.

meanings.note: Jordanian plural demonstrative for people: هدول البنات ('these/those girls').

examples.trans: Those girls are in our class.
Who are those people standing over there?

meanings.note: Singular بنت, definite البنت, plural بنات / البنات ('AlRawabi School for Girls' = مدرسة الروابي للبنات).

examples.trans: She is a very bright girl.
The girls are standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Negates nouns, adjectives, participles, prepositional phrases, and لازم (مش صح، مش معنا، مش قادرة، مش بعد اليوم).

examples.trans: This talk is not true.
I'm not upset with you.

meanings.note: Takes suffixes معي (with me), معك (with you), معها (with her), معنا (with us), معكم (with you all), معهم (with them), and forms مع السلامة! ('Goodbye!').

examples.trans: Come sit with us.
Goodbye, see you tomorrow!

meanings.note: Everyday loanword used across Jordan for the school bus (باص المدرسة); عالباص contracts على الباص.

examples.trans: We got on the bus in the morning.
The bus is parked outside.

meanings.note: Quintessential Levantine 'why?' (literally 'for what thing?': لـ + إيش).

examples.trans: Why were you late today?
I don't know why she got upset.

meanings.note: The main Levantine verb for 'talk / say / tell', far more common in Amman than تكلم.

examples.trans: Who told you the news?
Tell me what happened with you.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine manner word: ليش بتحكي هيك؟ ('why are you talking like that?'), زي هيك ('like this'), بعد هيك ('after this').

examples.trans: Don't talk to me like that.
That's not what we agreed on.

meanings.note: Placed before a name or title whenever addressing someone directly (يا دينا، يا مس فاتن); natural English usually drops it.

examples.trans: Come here, Mariam.
Thank you very much, Miss.

meanings.note: Derived from يا الله; urges action ('Come on, get off!') or wraps up warmly ('Alright, next time I'll come!').

examples.trans: Come on quickly, we'll be late!
Alright, we'll talk tomorrow.

meanings.note: Means both 'get off' a vehicle (انزلي من الباص) and 'go down' to the schoolyard (نزلت عالساحة).

examples.trans: We went down to the courtyard together.
Get off the bus calmly.

meanings.note: Takes pronoun endings مني (from me), منها (of/from her), منكم (of you): تكون من شلتها ('be part of her clique'), بخاف منها ('afraid of her').

examples.trans: I got off the bus.
Which one of you saw what happened?

meanings.note: High-frequency Levantine word for 'now' (contracted from هاد الوقت).

examples.trans: We have to go to class right now.
I feel a bit relieved now.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine pronunciation (daayman) of classical دائماً.

examples.trans: She always comes early.
We always sit here.

meanings.note: Construes with بـ or في: بتحكموا فينا ('you boss us around / control us').

examples.trans: I don't like anyone bossing me around.
Try to control your nerves.

meanings.note: Appears with pronoun endings like فينا in بتحكموا فينا ('you boss us around').

examples.trans: Nobody bosses us around.
I thought about you yesterday.

meanings.note: With حال + pronoun (عاملين حالهم عصابة), means 'acting like / pretending to be a gang'.

examples.trans: She's pretending she doesn't hear.
What are you up to today?

meanings.note: With suffixes, acts as the Levantine reflexive ('myself/themselves': حالهم), 'alone' (لحالك), and 'one's own business' (خليكم بحالكم).

examples.trans: I studied the lesson by myself.
Leave me to myself, please.

meanings.note: Mariam uses عصابة to describe how Layan's clique intimidates the whole school.

examples.trans: They act like a gang.
We aren't afraid of their gang.

meanings.note: Central setting: مدرسة الروابي للبنات ('AlRawabi School for Girls').

examples.trans: The school is close to our house.
I like going to school early.

meanings.note: Versatile Levantine word meaning 'but' between clauses and 'only / just' inside a clause.
As a focus adverb before a verb, noun, or imperative, بس narrows or softens the statement.

examples.trans: I tried to speak, but she didn't hear me.
I just want one minute.

meanings.note: Temporal preposition: مش بعد اليوم ('not after today') and بعد هيك ('after this').

examples.trans: We'll see you after class.
I won't stay quiet after today.

meanings.note: Indefinite كل يوم means 'every day'; definite اليوم means 'today' (مش بعد اليوم 'not after today').

examples.trans: We see each other every day at school.
Today the weather is very pleasant.

meanings.note: In the past مع ما (ما عرفت شو أعمل), means 'I didn't know what to do'; b-present بعرف means 'I know'.

examples.trans: I know this place well.
I didn't know how to answer the question.

meanings.note: Clause-linking particle taking pronoun suffixes directly: إني ('that I'), إنك ('that you').

examples.trans: I know that you're honest.
I thought that I was late.

meanings.note: هربتي من الباص accuses Mariam of sneaking off / skipping the school bus.

examples.trans: I have never skipped class.
We mustn't run away from responsibility.

meanings.note: Answers a question negatively ('no') or forms negative commands before a second-person subjunctive verb (لا تصدقوها! 'don't believe her!').

examples.trans: No Miss, that's not true.
Don't worry, everything is fine.

meanings.note: Standard Jordanian private-school address for a female teacher or principal, used alone (يا مس) or before her first name (مس فاتن، مس عبير).

examples.trans: Yes Miss, I'm ready.
Ms. Faten is in her office now.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine demonstrative used before a definite noun (هاد الإشي، هاد الحكي) or as a pronoun (حتى لو هاد آخر إشي).

examples.trans: Is this book yours?
This isn't fair at all.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of حكى; هاد الحكي means 'this talk / this claim'.

examples.trans: This talk is unacceptable.
I heard all the talk that happened.

meanings.note: Short, invariable spoken word for 'true / right' (مش صح 'not true', صح 'right!').

examples.trans: What you say is a hundred percent right.
This claim isn't true.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine word for 'who?' in both direct and indirect questions (مين حكى إلك؟، بعرف مين عم بيحكي).

examples.trans: Who is standing at the door?
I don't know who took the pen.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine dative base taking pronoun endings: إلي (to me), إلك (to you), إلها (to her), إلنا (for us), إلهم (to them).

examples.trans: This book is for you.
Tell me the truth.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian word corresponding to formal شيء; definite form الإشي, plural أشياء.

examples.trans: There is something important I want to say.
Nothing happened.

meanings.note: Placed before a b-present verb (عم بكذبوا، عم بتتحديني) to spotlight an action happening right now.

examples.trans: The girls are studying in the library right now.
What are you saying?

meanings.note: Construes with على for lying to or about someone (كذبوا علي، عم بكذبوا عليكي).

examples.trans: I have never lied to you.
The girls are lying to the principal.

meanings.note: Takes pronoun endings: علي (on/about me), عليكي (to you, f.), عليها (to her), علينا (on/for us), عليكم (on you, pl.). Often contracts to عـ before الـ.

examples.trans: Count on me in this matter.
They lied about me in front of the teacher.

meanings.note: Used by teachers and students for a female classmate (زميلتك بالصف).

examples.trans: She is my classmate in the same class.
Respect your classmates at school.

meanings.note: عالصف contracts على الصف ('to class'), and بالصف means 'in class'.

examples.trans: Go back to class right now.
We are in the same class.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun, كل means 'every' (كل يوم، كل إشي); with الـ (الكل) it means 'everyone'; with suffixes (كلنا، كلهم، كلها) 'all of us/them/it'.

examples.trans: Everyone knows the story.
We see each other every day.

meanings.note: Used for an issue under discussion (هاد الموضوع، أي موضوع بالضبط؟).

examples.trans: Let's close this topic.
The matter is more serious than I thought.

meanings.note: Pairs with انتباه ('catch attention': لفت انتباهي) or نظر ('draw eyes': نلفت نظرهم).

examples.trans: Her words caught the principal's attention.
We don't want to draw anyone's attention.

meanings.note: Frequently paired with لفت ('caught my attention': لفت انتباهي).

examples.trans: This question caught my attention.
Thank you for your attention.

meanings.note: Appears in the classic Arabic farewell مع السلامة! ('Goodbye!', literally 'with safety').

examples.trans: Thank goodness you're safe.
Goodbye, Dina!
